title: Build a generic fixed-capacity ring buffer in Rust with push/pop/peek
description: Greenfield Rust task: implement a generic RingBuffer<T> with a fixed capacity that overwrites the oldest element when full. Support push, pop, peek, len, is_empty, and is_full.

task_spec.prompt:
Create src/lib.rs implementing a generic fixed-capacity ring buffer.

pub struct RingBuffer<T> { ... }  // internal fields are your choice

impl<T> RingBuffer<T> {
    pub fn new(capacity: usize) -> Self
    pub fn push(&mut self, val: T)     // if full, evict oldest before inserting
    pub fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<T> // remove and return oldest element
    pub fn peek(&self) -> Option<&T>   // borrow oldest without removing
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool
    pub fn is_full(&self) -> bool
}

Hint: std::collections::VecDeque is a convenient backing store.

All 5 tests in tests/ring_buffer_test.rs must pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: push evicts oldest when at capacity
pop returns and removes oldest element (FIFO)
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
